title: Star Wars Zero Company 开发商 Bit Reactor 裁员人数未披露
content:
Star Wars Zero Company developer Bit Reactor has laid off an unspecified number of people | GamesIndustry.biz

Read our editorial policy
.
Bit Reactor furloughed "
many of its workers
" ahead of the release of the turn-based tactics game Star Wars Zero Company in August, before starting the process of
returning furloughed staff to work in October
. Now, it has emerged that an unspecified number of workers at the developer have been laid off.
As reported by the Star Wars site
Bespin Bulletin
on Friday, various employees revealed that November 6 would be their last day at the studio. Since then, several former Bit Reactor employees have talked about their experiences on LinkedIn.
Environment artist Michael Cabezas confirmed on
LinkedIn
that he had been laid off from Bit Reactor, saying that working with the team on a Star Wars title was a "career highlight" for him, and that he was "proud of the work we were able to accomplish on Star Wars Zero Company".
QA professional Ryan Mosher also
confirmed
he had been laid off, along with producer
Michael Blackard
, environment artist
Joshua Jay
, UI engineer
Tyler Eichten
, and senior environment artist
Ryan Lopez
.
Bit Reactor was
founded just over four years ago in Maryland by former Firaxis art director Greg Foertsch
, drawing on talent from the XCOM developer as well as other studios. Zero Company was published by Electronic Arts, and launched on August 27 to favourable reviews, currently with
a score of 84 on Metacritic
for the PC release.
In late September, Alinea Analytics
estimated that Zero Company had sold a million units
, with nearly 70% of its sales coming from Steam (the game also launched on PS5 and Xbox). As of today, Video Game Insights estimates that Zero Company's sales total has now reached 1.2 million, generating approximately $52.2 million in revenue.
GamesIndustry.biz
has reached out to Bit Reactor and EA for comment, and we will update this story if we receive a response.
